date.note: Journal issue year; no month/day was captured from the fetched page.

title: Measurement of the Solar Electron Neutrino Flux with the Homestake Chlorine Detector

claim.quote: Measurement of the Solar Electron Neutrino Flux with the Homestake Chlorine Detector

summary.plain: The definitive summary of over two decades of Homestake data: solar neutrinos really were arriving at only about a third of the predicted rate, the original 'solar neutrino problem'.
summary.technical: Full-dataset (1970-1994) measurement of the solar-neutrino-induced 37Ar production rate: 2.56±0.16(stat)±0.16(syst) SNU.

why_it_matters.value: The definitive statement of the multi-decade chlorine-detector result that established the 'solar neutrino problem', motivating SNO, Super-Kamiokande, GALLEX/SAGE and eventually the discovery of neutrino oscillation.
why_it_matters.quote: a solar neutrino-induced 37Ar production rate of 2.56 ± 0.16 (statistical) ± 0.16 (systematic) SNU

key_value.note: SNU is not one of the atlas's recognised dimensions; recorded with dimension `count`/unit "" as the closest representation, true unit given in `display`.

significance.note: A rate measurement, not a discovery/observation/evidence claim with a single sigma; no significance figure applies.
